notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Xbox: a new Xbox tab plays original Xbox games with hakuX, from .iso (an XISO or a whole disc) or .chd files. It needs no BIOS and no hard disk image. Halo 2 runs at its full 30 frames a second. Each game has a Render resolution setting in Performance settings: 1x, the default, runs smoothest, and 2x is sharper. Xbox games have no save states.

Playing together: turn on System link (LAN) in a game's settings on every console to play its system link mode on your network, System Link in Halo 2 for example. Play Online in the game's menu does the same over the internet: one console hosts and gets a code, and the others join with it. Play Online turns system link on by itself. While system link is on, the pause menu leaves the game running, so the other players are not dropped.

Hidden games: the first game you hide on the web page sets a 4-digit PIN. Press both sticks in on the home screen and enter it to show hidden games; they hide again with the same press, at sleep or at a restart. Four wrong PINs lock it for six hours. A forgotten PIN can be replaced on the web page's Debug tab.

Wind Waker HD: a stick at rest no longer drifts. A game with no dead zone saved gets 10 percent, and one you set yourself is kept.

USB file transfer: a file that did not finish copying (the cable pulled, the copy cancelled or the drive full) is removed instead of being left cut off, and the console tells you which file to copy again.

Browse all files: when the SD card has turned read-only after an error, a delete or move says so and asks you to restart, in place of a bare error.

New and lightly tested: Xbox was tried with Halo 2 only. Two consoles played a System Link round on the same network and online, but no level was played through with a controller, and three or more players were not tried. The USB fix was not tried with a real cable pull.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
